title: Data Center Fair Share Act

latestAction.text: Approved P.L.2026, c.32

Identical to S731.
significance: Shifts grid and supply costs to large data centers and adds curtailment obligations, raising the cost and lowering the reliability profile of NJ service for hyperscale loads, while providing a capacity-offset pathway. Reported 85%-of-projected-cost minimum commitments for 50 MW+ facilities should be confirmed against BPU implementation.

title: Data centers; disclosure of expected water use

latestAction.text: Passed the General Assembly (per MultiState report); subsequently enacted as 2026 Acts of Assembly Chapter 623 (approval date not confirmed)

summary: Requires applicants for new data centers to disclose expected water use in a site assessment before rezoning or special use approval, or at site plan submission for by-right projects.
significance: Gives localities and water utilities water-demand information before approvals; no cap on use.

title: SCC evaluation of data center Tier 2 backup generators

latestAction.text: Reported as passed by the Senate and carried over to the 2027 session

summary: Requires the SCC to evaluate limiting data centers' use of Tier 2 diesel generators and prioritizing cleaner Tier 4 units.
significance: Northern Virginia's thousands of diesel backup generators are a growing air-quality issue; carried over to 2027.

latestAction.text: Reported as passed by the Senate and carried over to the 2027 session

title: Water supply; reporting of volumes supplied to data centers

latestAction.text: Passed the General Assembly (per MultiState report); subsequently enacted as 2026 Acts of Assembly Chapter 896 (approval date not confirmed)

summary: Requires water suppliers serving data centers that report withdrawal data to the State Water Control Board to report volumes supplied to data centers, including reclaimed water; effective Jan. 1, 2027.
significance: First statewide visibility into data center water consumption in the largest U.S. market.

title: An act relating to sustainable data center deployment

latestAction.text: House sustained the Governor's veto (83 yeas, 52 nays)

summary: Comprehensive data center siting and regulation bill (permitting standards, ratepayer protections and reporting for large data centers) that passed both chambers after House and Senate committee work.
significance: Vermont has no data center buildout pipeline of note; the veto leaves the state without a statutory framework. Its provisions are likely to be reintroduced in 2027.

title: An act relating to a temporary moratorium on AI data centers and a report on the construction and operation of AI data centers in Vermont

latestAction.text: Read first time and referred to the Committee on Finance

summary: Would impose a temporary moratorium on AI data centers in Vermont and require a report on their construction and operation.
significance: Received Senate Finance walk-throughs and testimony (Jan-Feb 2026) but never left committee; died at the end of the biennium.
caveats: Status mapped to failed because the 2025-2026 biennium adjourned without committee action.

title: Addressing emerging large energy use facilities

latestAction.text: Returned by resolution to the House Rules Committee for third reading

summary: Comprehensive regulation of large energy use facilities (data centers): utility service and cost-recovery requirements, clean energy and reporting obligations. Companion SB 6171.
significance: Passed the House 51-41 (Feb. 14, 2026) but stalled in Senate Ways & Means and died when the 2026 session adjourned; Washington's main 2026 data center action was instead the tax-exemption change in SB 6231.

title: Removing a tax exemption for the replacement of equipment for data centers

latestAction.text: Governor signed; Chapter 266, Laws of 2026

summary: Removes the sales and use tax exemption for replacement equipment at data centers (OFM request bill). Companion HB 2708.
significance: Raises lifecycle costs for existing Washington data centers (Quincy, Wenatchee, etc.) that refresh servers frequently; new-construction exemptions are not eliminated by this bill.

title: Relating to: certain requirements related to data centers

latestAction.text: Senate: failed to concur pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1

summary: Republican data center bill creating Wis. Stat. 196.20(10), 196.492 and 299.70: utility rate and cost-protection requirements for data centers and related environmental/water provisions. Companion SB 843.
significance: Passed the Assembly 53-44 (Jan. 20, 2026) but the Senate never concurred; died at the end of the floor period. Wisconsin is left with PSC-driven large-load tariffs (We Energies, Alliant) and local moratoriums.

title: Certified Microgrid Program (Power Generation and Consumption Act)

latestAction.text: Chapter 112, Acts, Regular Session, 2025

summary: Creates a certified microgrid program and certified high-impact data center districts allowing data centers to be powered by off-grid/behind-the-meter generation; limits county and municipal zoning and other restrictions on certified projects; directs a share of property tax revenue to state funds.
significance: One of the most developer-friendly statutes nationally: certified data centers and their microgrids are largely shielded from local land-use control, a priority of Gov. Morrisey.
